ev.q: The age-adjusted rates of hospital discharges among persons with LEA who had diabetes were 28 times that of those without diabetes
LEA rates increased with age in both populations, but rates were higher in the population with diabetes
Patients with diabetes-related LEA hospital discharges had a mean age of 66 years
In 1997, 131,218 hospital discharges had an LEA discharge diagnosis code; 87,720 (67%) of these were related to diabetes
Among persons with diabetes, approximately 52% of amputations occurred at or below the foot
the age-adjusted rates of hospital discharges among persons with LEA who had diabetes were 28 times that of those without diabetes
Age-adjusted LEA rates were much higher for persons with diabetes for both sexes and all racial/ethnic populations
Hospital discharges were estimated from NIS, a stratified probability sample of hospitals in 22 states.
Estimates of the number of persons with and without diabetes were obtained from the 1997 NHIS

methods_quotes.q: SUDAAN was used to calculate estimates and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) of NIS and NHIS data.
The 2000 U.S. standard population was used to adjust LEA rates by age.
The rate ratio was calculated by dividing the LEA rate for persons with diabetes by the rate for persons without diabetes.
The significance of trends by age was assessed for LEA rates, rate ratios, and rate differences
t-tests in SUDAAN were used to determine the significance of the difference in mean age by diabetes status
Z-tests were used to assess the difference between age-adjusted rates by diabetes status among all sex and race groups.
